headline: Dubai Oil Benchmark Slips Into Contango Amid Rising Middle East Supply
summary: The Dubai oil benchmark curve slipped into contango for the first time since July as rising physical flows from Middle East Gulf producers exceed current demand.
why: The Dubai benchmark is a key pricing reference for sour crude oil produced in the Middle East and exported to Asia, serving as a vital gauge of regional supply and demand balances for professional energy traders.

impacts.name: Dubai Crude
impacts.why: An oversupply and shift into contango indicates near-term physical surplus, weighing on prompt pricing relative to future deliveries.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: The shift into contango reflects rising physical oil flows from Gulf producers exceeding current demand, signaling ample near-term supply in the region.
